images.seen: A warm-night balcony — sweating jug of ice water and two glasses on the table, woven hand fan on the chair, sheer curtain billowing, palms beyond the rail. Thursday.
lines: The curtain is moving, which is the first good news since this morning.
Ice in the jug, fan on the chair: the night shift of a forty-degree day.
The first breeze in twelve hours just walked in without knocking.

images.seen: A pedestal fan running beside the bed at 2:00 AM, someone asleep under a mosquito net, glass of water on the nightstand. Monday.
lines: Two in the morning and the fan is the hardest worker in the house.
The fan is on its third shift and the night is still not cooling.
The glass on the nightstand went warm an hour ago; the fan carries on alone.

images.seen: Friends in the pool at night with drinks under string lights, one more watching from the deck, the house glowing warm behind. Saturday.
lines: Still thirty degrees after dark, so the party moved into the water.
Night swimming is not a plan; it is what this weather leaves you.
The day never cooled, so the drinks came to the shallow end.

images.seen: A labrador lying flat on the cool bathroom tiles at night, freestanding bath behind, warm passage light falling across the floor. Wednesday.
lines: The lab did a full survey and the bathroom tiles won by two degrees.
Tile is the coldest surface in the house tonight, and it is taken.
The dog knows where the house keeps its last cool square metres.
